html:
The first mint in the Americas, set up by royal order in Mexico City in 1535 under the first viceroy of New Spain, Antonio de Mendoza. It still runs today as the Mexican Mint.

It struck silver from the mines of Zacatecas and Guanajuato, which in time outproduced even Potosí. Its most famous coin was the piece of eight, worth eight reales, also called the Spanish dollar.

That coin became the first world currency:

  • The treasure fleets carried it to Spain, from where it spread across Europe.
  • The Manila galleons carried it across the Pacific to the Philippines, where it paid for Chinese silk and porcelain. Ming China, which taxed in silver, soaked it up.
  • It was legal money in the United States until 1857, and the US dollar was based on it.

Later Mexican pesos kept the same weight, and they circulated in China into the 1900s.
